hypothesis: Fresh completed-five-minute ETH breakout onsets filtered by prior one-minute BBWP compression and a directional pullback may retain a small repeatable edge after live taker friction with a 60-bps protective stop and 12-hour maximum hold.
decision: Retain the exact ETH v12 candidate in report-only observation. Its first non-overlapping forward path resolved positive after modeled round-trip friction and official funding, and it was compatible with the observed shared-portfolio state. One counterfactual path is insufficient to estimate repeatability, drawdown, side robustness, or venue execution quality, so it receives no execution authority and is not promoted by this revision.
falsifier: The hypothesis is weakened or rejected if subsequent profile-matched, non-overlapping long and short paths erase the 40.96-bps initial surplus, or if actual venue fills show materially worse friction than the 13-bps model. Runtime parity is falsified by any mismatch in completed-bar onset identity, prior compression, directional pullback, one-position-per-coin routing, stop placement, funding attribution, or maximum-hold timing.
limitations: The single resolved candidate cannot establish a stable win rate, profit factor, drawdown, cadence, or side-specific edge.
The observation used completed one-minute candles and cannot reproduce intrabar stop ordering or actual IOC fill slippage.
The decision reference is not proof that a real order would have filled at the modeled entry price.
The simulated outcome is non-additive and is excluded from live portfolio performance.
The historical entry and stop/hold selections were post-hoc; this forward path tests implementation consistency but does not remove selection bias.
No strategy, live position, order, allocation, or execution authority changed in this revision.
